authorized_evidence.content:
Privileged Access Review

Privileged access must be reviewed monthly for production systems and quarterly for business applications. Reviewers must confirm business need, manager approval, and least-privilege alignment.

Privileged access exceptions require an owner, expiration date, and documented business justification.

Release Windows

Standard production deployments occur Tuesday through Thursday between 10:00 and 15:00 Eastern Time. Deployments outside that window require approval from the Engineering Manager on call and a written reason in the change record.

Friday deployments are limited to severity-one fixes, security patches approved by IT Admin, or customer-impacting incidents where waiting would increase risk. Weekend deployments require the incident commander to approve the change before execution.

Access Notice

This document is restricted to IT/Admin users. It contains operational security guidance and must not be summarized for unauthorized roles.

On-Call Severity Levels

| Severity | Definition | Initial Response Target |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| SEV-1 | Widespread production outage or data exposure risk | 15 minutes |
| SEV-2 | Major workflow unavailable for multiple customers | 30 minutes |
| SEV-3 | Degraded feature with workaround available | 4 business hours |
| SEV-4 | Low-impact defect or documentation issue | Next planning cycle |

The on-call engineer owns triage until an incident commander is assigned. The incident commander owns status updates, escalation, and post-incident review scheduling.

Incident Triage

Security incidents are triaged by impact, affected systems, data classification, and containment status. The exact severity scoring formula is not published in this knowledge base.

IT/Admin users should record incident timeline, containment steps, affected data categories, and communication owner.

The passage 'SEV-1 | Widespread production outage or data exposure risk | 15 minutes' entails that a widespread production outage is SEV-1.
The same passage states the initial response target for SEV-1 is 15 minutes, which applies to a widespread production outage.
